name: Harry French
expNote: CV shows contract to 2026; Leicester offered a 2-year deal - confirm current expiry
notes: Left-footed GK, 194cm, Leicester academy, England U17. Looking for a first senior loan (Liam target list: League Two, National League, NL North, NL South).
cvProfile: Commanding left-footed goalkeeper at 194cm. Dominant in his box with an elite distribution range and the footwork to play out from the back. Leicester City academy, capped by England at U17.

reasons: Cowley plays a structured build-from-the-back game that suits a ball-playing keeper, and the No.1 shirt is genuinely open. Stable mid-table L2, strong development environment.
GK need HIGH: No.1 Matt Macey departing (released, May 2026) after a Golden Glove season, leaving a true vacancy.
Caveat: a 20yo replacing a multi-award keeper is a big ask; Cowley is also scouting senior options. Pitch him as first-choice ready, not a project.

The cleanest pattern match: Ayr took Max Thompson (Newcastle) on loan in Jan 2026 and habitually use young English/academy loan keepers. Championship level is a realistic No.1 push; possession side suits his distribution. No work permit needed (UK).
GK need HIGH: Thompson's loan ends June 2026 and he returns to Newcastle; the rest are backup level.
Caveat: they may re-loan another known EFL keeper from their pipeline.
Explicitly runs the young-loan-keeper model: 2025-26 No.1 was Matty Young (Sunderland, b.2006), brought in to develop. Well-funded promotion side, his template exactly.
GK need HIGH: Young's loan ends and he returns to Sunderland; Salford need a new keeper.
Caveat: manager Karl Robinson was sacked (June 2026), so the new boss could reset recruitment, and a near-promotion side may want experience.
Actively in the market for a keeper and has used English loan keepers (Oxborough/Motherwell). Competitive top-half Championship side, real senior minutes. No work permit needed (UK).
GK need HIGH: No.1 Deniz Mehmet (33) out of contract end-May 2026; only a teenager behind him, and the club has stated it needs to add a keeper.
Caveat: if Mehmet re-signs as the experienced head, French competes/develops rather than walks in.
Paul Cook's ambitious, well-backed L2 promotion side that openly uses young loan keepers (Max Thompson was their No.1). Proven pathway for a loanee to start in a winning team.
GK need MEDIUM-HIGH: Thompson (Newcastle loan) returns to parent; only an experienced No.2 behind him (inferred from loan ending).
Caveat: incumbent Ryan Boot could be handed the shirt; a promotion chaser may prefer a proven senior keeper.
Genuine No.1 vacancy at a parachute-budget club intent on returning to the EFL; a commanding ball-playing keeper would start from day one.
GK need HIGH: keeper Harry Isted not offered a new deal (released list, 2026).
Caveat: unsettled post-relegation environment; promotion pressure may push them to an experienced NL keeper.
Keeper department gutted after a double relegation; a strong young keeper walks into first-team football and dominates a division at a big-for-the-level club. No work permit needed (UK).
GK need HIGH: No.1 Ross Laidlaw (33) leaving, second keeper joined Burton; only an 18yo signed so far. They need a senior keeper.
Caveat: League One is a step down in level/profile; sell it as guaranteed minutes, not a shop window.
Newly stabilised big NL club aiming for the EFL, with the keeper position just opened up and a strong platform for a young keeper to establish himself.
GK need HIGH: No.1 Nick Hayes left for Hartlepool (permanent), creating a vacancy.
Caveat: confirm they haven't already signed a senior keeper; ambition may favour experience.
Big-budget former EFL club that just missed promotion and used a loan keeper last season (Archie Mair/Morecambe), so the loan route is established. Will push again.
GK need MEDIUM: Mair's short-term loan ends and he returns to parent; they need to settle the position with an upgrade (inferred).
Caveat: a promotion-desperate club may want a seasoned NL keeper over a debutant.
Use loan keepers (Budinauckas from Rangers) and play an expansive possession style that suits elite distribution; promotion-chasing, high-quality minutes. No work permit needed (UK).
GK need MEDIUM-HIGH: Budinauckas listed among departures (squad update, late May 2026), opening the No.1 spot.
Caveat: a promotion favourite will want a keeper they trust immediately; expect competition for the shirt.
Resurgent, ambitious NL club; a starting-calibre young keeper who commands the box and distributes would compete immediately.
GK need MEDIUM: thin, unsettled keeper group (Owen Foster out of contract June 2026) (inferred, not a confirmed No.1 exit).
Caveat: weakest evidence in this tier - Louis Jones could be retained as No.1.
Relegated and rebuilding; clearly trusts and plays loan keepers (2025-26 No.1 was Harvey Davies, Liverpool). A young keeper could be first choice straight away.
GK need HIGH: Davies' loan ends and returns to parent; the position needs a starter.
Caveat: a relegated club in structural flux is riskier, and NL is a modest level - but the minutes are real.
Unstable keeper position all season; a commanding young keeper would push hard for the shirt at a club rebuilding its spine, with L2 minutes if he wins it.
GK need MEDIUM-HIGH: No.1 Nik Tzanev left mid-season (to Huddersfield, Feb 2026); multiple loans returned (inferred instability).
Caveat: a club that just survived may default to an experienced keeper; confirm their summer plan.

Already runs a British loan keeper (Evan Watts on loan from Swansea), so the model is proven and they are comfortable with the route. No work permit needed (Common Travel Area). LOI Premier is competitive senior football.
GK need LOW-MEDIUM: Watts is the current No.1 and wants to stay, so this is a contingency/competition play unless he is recalled in the summer window (mid-season).
Caveat: no hard vacancy now; keep warm rather than lead with it.
Just promoted to tier 5 and will need to upgrade the goalkeeping department for the higher level; pathway to first-choice in a fresh, ambitious squad.
GK need MEDIUM: promotion typically triggers a GK upgrade (inferred, not a confirmed exit).
Caveat: they may simply keep their promotion-winning keeper; smaller platform.
Strong history of taking young English-developed keepers (signed George Shelvey, ex-Forest); open to the British pathway. No work permit needed (CTA). Mid-season loan possible.
GK need MEDIUM: rely on a loanee (Conor Kearns, injury-hit) plus a 42yo backup - fragile depth, a summer addition is plausible (inferred).
Caveat: depth may be considered full unless Kearns' fitness/loan status changes.
Hinshelwood's Worthing are an attractive possession-based, build-from-the-back side - an ideal style fit for a ball-playing keeper - now stepping up to tier 5.
GK need LOW-MEDIUM: promotion upgrade plausible but unconfirmed (inferred).
Caveat: speculative vacancy; they may retain their title-winning keeper. Modest level, but the style is perfect.
Top-flight environment with a strong goalkeeping culture; a high-ceiling young keeper could be added as a development No.2 with a pathway if the No.1 moves on. No work permit needed (UK).
GK need LOW-MEDIUM: Robby McCrorie is first-choice (signed 2025), so this is a development signing, not immediate minutes (inferred).
Caveat: little realistic senior football in year one unless McCrorie leaves.
Actively recruit English keepers (current No.1 Sam Sargeant, ex-Leyton Orient), so they understand his profile; a struggling side is a place to win the shirt. No work permit needed (CTA).
GK need MEDIUM (timed late): Sargeant contracted only to end-2026, so the real opening is the close-season (late 2026 / early 2027).
Caveat: wrong timing for an immediate summer-2026 move; a pre-contract / early-2027 target.
Promoted and ambitious, will need to raise quality across the squad including goalkeeper for tier 5; realistic first-choice opportunity with games if he wins it.
GK need LOW-MEDIUM: promotion-driven upgrade likely but unconfirmed (inferred).
Caveat: smallest platform here and the vacancy is speculative; a fallback.

The one clean continental easy win: as a British citizen he needs NO work permit in Gibraltar, and squads here are heavily foreign with constant European-rotation turnover. Perennial champions and Gibraltar's UEFA entrant.
GK need MEDIUM (inferred): ageing import No.1 and deep European-rotation demand make a young 194cm distributor a credible add. No contact in book yet, approach via the club's sporting structure.

Caveat: low standard and minimal profile; likely a No.2/development role behind a keeper trusted for European qualifiers. (Malta is the other viable route - streamlined non-EU permit - if a specific club has a June-2026 vacancy.)

name: Tommy Neale
notes: Technical No.8, Leicester academy U11 to U21, England U17-U18. 2025/26: 26 apps, 1 goal, 3 assists, 1,913 mins (U21). Looking for a first senior loan.
cvProfile: Technical central midfielder who dictates tempo. Comfortable receiving under pressure and breaking lines, with the positional intelligence to play across all three midfield positions. Leicester City academy from U11 to U21, England U17 to U18.
